items.title: The miners go back
items.line: The miners' strike ended on 3 March 1985 after almost a year. Many pits marched back behind brass bands, and Britain's 175 working pits of 1983 had all closed by the end of 2015.

items.title: EastEnders
items.line: Julia Smith and Tony Holland's soap set in Albert Square started on BBC One on 19 February 1985. More than 30 million watched the Christmas Day episode the following year.

items.title: Sinclair C5
items.line: Sinclair launched its £399 electric trike at Alexandra Palace on 10 January 1985. Top speed 15 mph; production stopped in August after about 5,000 of 14,000 sold.

items.title: The black ball final
items.line: Dennis Taylor beat Steve Davis 18-17 on the final black on 28 April 1985. BBC2 coverage ended at 12:23 a.m. with 18.5 million watching, a UK record after midnight.

items.title: Live Aid
items.line: Wembley (72,000) and JFK Stadium in Philadelphia (89,484) on 13 July 1985, with an estimated 1.9 billion watching in 150 countries. Sade, Bryan Ferry and Paul Young all played the London show.

items.title: Brothers in Arms
items.line: Dire Straits released it on 17 May 1985, fully digitally recorded at AIR Montserrat and the Power Station. It was the first album to sell a million copies on CD.

items.title: Back to the Future
items.line: It opened in the US on 3 July 1985. It cost $19 million and was the highest-grossing film of the year worldwide.
